label: first occurrence of l/c (also 2,q,3,o) early in the original phase
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t <= 5) & (in_first == 1) & isin(in_tok, [tok("l"), tok("c"), tok("2"), tok("q"), tok("3"), tok("o")])
explanation: Original-phase token detector: 98% of activation mass is in the original phase, and almost none at the delimiter or during copy. It fires on the first occurrence of an input token (in_first=1 holds 96% of mass), mostly at positions t=1..4 (t=2,3 carry over 60% of mass), and favours specific tokens: l (6.0x lift) and c (5.6x) most strongly, then 2, q, 3, o, w, k, v. Magnitude is largest for l/c at t=3 when the sequence starts with f/g/j/0, where top activations reach ~1.0 of max. Activation is weaker for repeated tokens and late positions (t>=6), and it is essentially silent in the copy phase. Firing is context-dependent: the same token at the same position is often inactive (precision ~0.4), and many weak activations land on other tokens, so the token-and-position predicate is only a partial description (dev F1 0.47, mass recall 0.69).
